title: Autor: why ATMs raised teller employment
summary: ATMs automated the routine part of a teller's day, which freed tellers for advice and relationships and cut the cost of a branch, so banks opened many more branches. Tellers per branch fell but total tellers rose from about 300,000 to 500,000. If a job is almost entirely routine there is no residual human task and it is eliminated.
source: Ch09 §9.2 — David Autor, the ATM paradox and task bundles

nodes.label: Residual Human Tasks
nodes.description: Advice, relationships, judgment that stay with people

edges.description: Automation lowers the labor cost of a branch
Fewer tellers are needed per branch
Automating the routine part frees the human part
A job with residual human tasks transforms rather than vanishes

identifiability_note: Observed labor-market series; the critical variable is the composition of the task bundle.
